newsitem.title: GHANA: Malaysian firm seeks stake in Ghana film industry.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firm seeks stake in Ghana film industry.

text.p: A Malaysian film production company has made an offer for a 70 percent stake in the state-run Ghana Film Industry Corporation (GFIC).
GFIC Managing director Victor Anti told Reuters on Friday that Sistem Televisyen Malaysia Berhad had pledged this month to invest $100 million in the company over five years in return for the stake.
"The GFIC needs recapitalisation to modernise equipment which will be used to produce, rent out and used in joint ventures," Deputy Information Minister Kojo Yankah told a news conference earlier.

Negotiations were at an advanced stage, the minister said but he declined to give details on timing or the price offered by the company for the stake. Ghana's government will keep a 30 percent stake in what is Ghana's only film production company.

Anti said the company produced four feature films a year with a 800 billion cedi ($470,000) budget, 139 employees and assets worth about $2 million. The government pays 60 percent of GFIC's budget but will stop when a private investor has been found.
GFIC made "Cobra Verde" with producer Werner Herzog in 1987 about women warriors in the pre-colonial kingdom of Dahomey.
In 1994, producer Peter Kosminsky of "Wuthering Heights" fame used GFIC for the making of "The Dying of the Light" about the killing of a U.N. volunteer in Somalia.
GFIC played an active role in the 1995 production of "Deadly Voyage", a movie about a group of nine Ghanaian stowaways of whom one survived to tell of murder on the high seas.
